findings: A1: `## Build plan` is absent by design, not by omission. generate_instruction.md 2.1 removes it from the baseline emission and [metadata].spec_sections_given records the exclusion, so A1's eleven-section list is stale against the current contract. Every rubric-parsed H2 is present and canonically spelled (G33 PASS). Routes to the prompt, not to the brief.
B3: the same divergence. The emitted lever sections are those the baseline carries; the withheld one is recorded in spec_sections_given rather than lost.

C5: the check asks for concurrency invariants named as a storage-level construct -- a unique or partial-unique index, a transaction. INV9 and G43 forbid that vocabulary in `## Data model`, and G43 PASSES on this brief. The capacity invariants are stated as observable properties instead ('committed days equal the sum over that window's bookings, always, and never exceed capacity days'), which is the substitution 4.0 mandates.

C7: `## Core features` (16.9k), `## UI/UX notes` (11.7k) and `## Front-end specification` (8.6k) run past the judge's 2,500-char per-section slice, reported by flag_lint as a WARN. Recorded as a WARN, not a FAIL: G33 and reference/L L.3.2 retired the length failure deliberately, the brief has no limit, and every judged criterion carries its own facts (G52 PASS), so the slice costs a diagnostic number rather than reward. No rule was cut to fit.

C9 numbering: `## Core features` was reordered during this pass so its 67 rules ascend in document order. Three subsections had been appended out of sequence and rules 65-67 sat under a heading that did not describe them; the blocks moved whole, rule 32a folded into rule 32, and rules 65-67 gained their own `### Instrumentation` heading. No obligation changed.

D4: the only sentence naming an external checker is the mandated Data-model line `so a grader can sign in`. It names no backing service and does not locate the checker outside the app's code, so it fails limb (b) of the BLOCKER test. Not a finding.

D5: companion contradiction sweep run over every design, motion, layout and accessibility sentence against yannesidibe_prd.md. No inversion found: the outline-over-fill display rule, the one-signature-curve motion rule, the drawn-over-faded stroke rule, the two-ground alternation and the reduced-motion rest-state rule all carry the source's sense rather than its opposite. The one deliberate departure is the twenty hand-tuned media queries, which the brief collapses to four and states as a defect it is fixing rather than a rule it is inverting.

D6 source carriage: G51 PASSES with 18/18 source colours described by family and tone, 272/272 topics carried and 752/752 enumerated items carried. Fifty items are carried by declared waiver in four classes -- the companion's own authoring apparatus, the design token value sheets the number rule keeps out of a brief, identifiers the lint renders unmatchable by stripping their underscores, and the two reference bodies scoped out in `## Constraints`. Each waiver is on the record in the sweep receipt.

S1-S10, B1-B2, G1-G3 answered against the seven documents in `_spec/S_booki_book_freelance-availability-booking-vb_20260916_071327/`. The spec is author-side and reaches no grader; `06-implementation-plan.md` states at its head that `## Build plan` is not emitted at this variant, so nothing in it leaks into the brief (G44 PASS).

G2: the API endpoint table, the six enquiry fields with their bounds and pinned error copy, the four budget bands, the ten mail subjects and the three seeded windows all round-trip between `01-PRD.md`, `03-app-flow.md`, `05-backend-schema.md` and the brief. The literals bijection is proved mechanically by G6, which PASSES over 161 pinned values.
S3: `02-TRD.md` carries the stack together with the no-second-store constraint, so the single-backing-service rule is stated author-side as well as in the brief.

BP-005: single-stage is correct here and is not a finding. Under `[verifier].environment_mode = "shared"` the grader runs in this same image, so the Python toolchain and the browser cannot be staged out of the final layer.
SEC-003: the image runs as root. No source establishes non-root execution, and the agent writes its application into /app during the session.

ARCH-002/ARCH-003: every image is pinned by explicit version TAG, which is the multi-architecture manifest list -- python:3.12-slim-bookworm, postgres:16.4-bookworm and axllent/mailpit:v1.30.6. No digest is pinned and none is fabricated, and the file declares `ARG TARGETARCH` without branching on it.

BP-004: the only build-time download is the NodeSource repository key, fetched over TLS, dearmored to a keyring and bound to the repository with `signed-by=`. That is the integrity mechanism the source provides; no checksum is published to verify against.
DEP-005: the Chromium package names are the bookworm set, matching CHROMIUM_LIBS in runtime_deps_lint.py, and the base is bookworm rather than trixie. G55 PASSES.

DEP-002: the application's own framework packages are deliberately NOT preinstalled. The brief names Svelte, Vite and Hono, and the agent resolves them in-build from its own package.json under `network_mode = "public"`; a globally pinned copy would clash with whatever the agent's manifest resolves. A global `vite` pin was written during this pass and removed for exactly that reason. Only the grader runtime, the browser and an up-to-date npm are baked in.

C1/C11/C12: `[metadata.services]` declares `backend = postgres` and `email = mailpit`, and the compose file carries a service of each name. The `main` service is present, sets `extra_hosts` and `ports`, and sets none of image, command, entrypoint or profiles.

RC-01: 120 checklist items carry the judgment-class `ui` tag. 77 of them are claimed by a judged criterion and 43 are driven by a browser substep -- walkable presence and behaviour checks a grader can perform without an opinion (does the band appear, does the slide-over open, does the empty state read its own line). That split is INV7 rather than an uncovered ask, and G28/G29 PASSES on it in both directions.

RC-15: converged on cycle 3 of 3. Cycle 1 authored 23 criteria; cycle 2 rewrote every criterion to the mechanical battery, removing six pronouns, two banned adverbs, one connector and three negations; cycle 3 rebuilt the set against the dimension budget, which had sat at ui_visual 0.47 with functionality empty and now sits at instruction_following 0.32, functionality 0.27, ux_flow 0.16 and ui_visual 0.15.

RC-16: every criterion opens differently and no rule sentence is reused. The shared `Answer yes when ... Answer no when ...` frame is the binary contract RC-09 and recompute.py both require, not a template: the claim and the enumerated no-cases differ per criterion, and G52 PASSES its surface-naming check at 23 of 23.

RC-06: each criterion names the surface a judge should look at in the brief's own words -- the fixed top bar, the first screen of the home page, the contact page, the work page, the studio's pipeline page. No criterion points at the brief, names a section, or carries a path.

The prompt declares no numbered check registry; its layer-1 partner checklist_qc.py PASSES (structure, ids, citations, ledger arithmetic). Adjudicated by reading: 522 items at core-ask granularity over 180 core asks, every one cited by exactly one channel (G28/G29 PASS) and every one covered by a grader in both directions (G24 PASS, 180 of 180 core asks fully graded).
